changes.final: \margin{On a deux façons de ``récupérer'' l'opération de $\Gamma$ sur le groupoïde $\widehat{\Pi}_1(X,I)$ (où $I\subset X_K$) en quelque sorte duales l'une de l'autre: soit on prend un syst. de $l_j:x_j\mathbin{-}y_j$ $(x_j,y_j\in I)$ générateurs pour $\Pi_1(X,I)$, et regarde les $f_{l_j}(u)$ ou $g_{l_j}(u)$, soit on fixe des $T_\alpha$ comme dessus, et on regarde les $g^\alpha_{x,y}$ $(\alpha\in A,x,y\in T_\alpha\cap I)$. En fait on voit très bientôt qu'il est \deleted{\unsure{ff}} inutile de supposer que les $T_\alpha$ recouvrent $X$ (p.ex. si les $T_\alpha$ sont les supports des chemins $l_j$).}

notes: Upright manuscript sheet, author number 6 at top and separate lower-right foliation 76. No printed block or reused typescript is present. The 76 is in a thinner hand than the body; attribution is left unnamed (archive foliation).
The opening continues an argument: effective paths decompose into direct pieces, and a descent argument is cited for the closed-X_alpha case. This page does not supply that descent proof.

The central paragraph generalizes to compatible nonempty I_alpha subsets of T_alpha, normally finite, and describes reconstruction from g^alpha_{y,x}. Its sentence stops after dans before a horizontal separator; no completion has been invented.

The oblique margin gives two ways of recovering the Gamma action on a fundamental groupoid: generators l_j or local T_alpha data. Its first Pi is hatted and its second is not. It says the covering assumption can be dropped, with the supports of the l_j as an example. These claims were transcribed, not proved.
The final paragraph explicitly keeps both X and u fixed before considering variable u in Gamma. It ends with the plural les formules and continues beyond this page; no other page was read.

Mathematical examination was confined to internal notation and the visible attachment/order of symbols: arrow terminal strokes, cancelled versus surviving g subscripts, f_l insertion, and capital/hatted groupoid notation. No theorem or proof was checked. Accordingly check_events is empty rather than reporting transcription as proof work.

Whole image was viewed once for layout, followed by top and bottom native-resolution halves once each. Seven crops were made for open places, all from original pixels by the supplied script. The margin crop was rotated -64 degrees; the other crops are unrotated. No OCR, web research or TeX compilation was used.
Six assigned MARKS rows were decided. Three additional C doubts not listed in MARKS were also examined: deleted chemins is resolved; cancelled yx and ff remain uncertain.

The first/last chain arrow interpretation and omission of C's extra que after voit were independently corroborated by root on existing crops during this return. The small hooked join after I_beta remains explicitly unresolved.

Root subsequently inspected the deleted chemins, final fixes and cancelled g subscript crops, and reported no new concerns beyond the shared et/comma uncertainty. The cancelled fragments still retain their explicit doubt marks.

Main reader compared the 19 inventory elements with the page layout and consolidated text. All reported disagreements were reviewed on the saved crops (16 additional review crops). The empty continuation after dans is preserved; the later paragraph is separated by the drawn rule. The phrase after I_beta and the cancelled yx and ff remain uncertain.

Apparatus completeness check: the three deleted C doubts, already decided in the reading and audit, are also listed explicitly in the supplementary decision table. This is a documentation completion only; no page reading changed.
